findings.title: canManage() grants manage permission with only view scope
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the method calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). The hasPermission method returns true if any of the provided scopes is granted. Therefore, a user with only the VIEW scope on all groups would be considered as having manage permission for all groups. This bypasses authorization checks that rely on requireManage() (e.g., creating groups, updating group management). The correct call should be hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) only.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs and uses wrong lookup
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code iterates over group resources and for each groupResource calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS) and then adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource ID, not the group ID. The method is expected to return a set of group IDs (as used by UserModel.GROUPS attribute in user search). Additionally, inside hasPermission, the lookup uses resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), but the group resource name is the group ID (set by AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup which returns group.getId()). Since the passed ID is the resource ID, the lookup will fail and fall back to the all-groups resource for every group, leading to incorrect permission evaluation. The correct approach is to use groupResource.getName() (which is the group ID) for both the permission check and the returned set.
